land.text: Messenia, the helot land of Sparta since the Messenian Wars

predecessors.note: The Messene page: after Leuctra (371) 'the helots of Messenia revolted yet again against their Spartan overlords'; Epaminondas built Messene in 369 and 'invited the return of the previous inhabitants and their descendants'. The Spartan state is written as peloponnesian-league (eu-01-c).

land.text: Messenia: 'Later Hypana in Elis, Corone, Messene, Sparta and Pagae ... were joined by conquest'

successors.note: The Achaean League page gives no date for Messene's entry; -191 is a bridging date shared with the achaean-league dossier. The Philopoemen page shows Messene a League member that revolts in 183 (Dinocrates).

capitals.name: Messene (Ithome)
capitals.note: 'Epaminondas built the new city of Messene on the site in 369 BC over the ruins of Ithome'; the walled circuit is 9 km long.

correction.text: Messenia, the south-western Peloponnese, from the foundation of Messene in 369

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Messene row; Messenia is drawn inside the Greek City-States aggregate (and, in -366..-362, in the Theban sphere, eu-01-c). The pages opened give no territory for the polis: the Messene page has only the city wall ('a circuit wall 9 km (5.6 mi) long'), the Messenia page only the modern regional unit (2,991 km2). The shape is the region Messenia, the land Sparta held as helot land since the Messenian Wars. Philip II's border gifts and the Dentheliatis are not on the pages opened.

region.text: Messenia, the south-western Peloponnese (modern regional unit 2,991 km2)

ledger.note: 369: Epaminondas founds Messene and Messenia is free of Sparta. 'Epaminondas built the new city of Messene on the site in 369 BC over the ruins of Ithome'; the exiles 'returned primarily from Sicily and North Africa'. The page names the city and the year; the land (all Messenia) is the reading of the Messenia page ('conquered and enslaved as helots by ancient Sparta').

region.text: Messenia, the south-western Peloponnese (modern regional unit 2,991 km2)

ledger.note: 201: Nabis of Sparta seizes Messene. 'In 201 BC, Nabis invaded and captured Messene.' The same page also has Philopoemen expelling Nabis 'from Messene' in a sentence it places at 205 BC; the two dates conflict.

region.text: Messenia, the south-western Peloponnese (modern regional unit 2,991 km2)

ledger.note: Nabis is driven out: 'the Spartans were forced to retreat when the Achaean League army under Philopoemen intervened'. The page gives no year for the retreat (and a sentence at 205 BC); -200 is a bridging date.

region.text: Messenia, the south-western Peloponnese (modern regional unit 2,991 km2)

ledger.note: 191: Messene enters the Achaean League. 'Later Hypana in Elis, Corone, Messene, Sparta and Pagae in Attica were joined by conquest' (sic); no date on the page. Bridging date: between Nabis' retreat and the revolt of 183 against the League (Philopoemen page); -191 matches the achaean-league dossier.

region.text: Messenia, the south-western Peloponnese (modern regional unit 2,991 km2)

ledger.note: 191: Messenia passes to the Achaean League and the independent Messene ends; Dinocrates' revolt of 183 ('encouraged Messene to revolt against the League') and the League's capture of the city are recorded in achaean-league (contest 183-182); the page's wording: 'the members of the Achaean League joined forces to capture Messene' after Philopoemen was captured and killed there.

wars.name: Nabis' capture of Messene

zones.text: Messenia, the south-western Peloponnese (modern regional unit 2,991 km2)

wars.outcome: Nabis captured Messene in 201 BC; the Spartans retreated when Philopoemen's Achaean army intervened.
wars.note: The page also puts Philopoemen's expulsion of Nabis at 205 BC; the years conflict and the end year is a bridge.

certainty.note: No page dates a frontier of the Messenian polis; the line with Laconia, Arcadia and Elis is approximate throughout.

sources.title: Messene

sources.title: Messenia
sources.note: Spartan conquest and helotage; modern regional unit 2,991 km2; silent on 369 and on the later polis.

sources.title: Achaean League
sources.note: 'Messene ... joined by conquest' (undated); Sparta forced in by Philopoemen; 146 dissolution.

sources.title: Philopoemen
sources.note: 201 Nabis captures Messene, Philopoemen intervenes; 183 Dinocrates' revolt, Philopoemen killed at Messene, the League captures Messene.

notes: Messene is the Messenian polis that Epaminondas founded in 369 and that the Achaean League absorbed. The pages opened (Messene, Messenia, Achaean League, Philopoemen) give no area for the polis and no frontier; the shape is the region Messenia (Messenia is not in the gazetteer: listed as needed, with the place Messene). The end year -191 is a bridging date (confidence 1): the Achaean League page says Messene was 'joined by conquest' without a date, and the Philopoemen page shows it a League member revolting in 183, so the entry lies between about 200 and 183; achaean-league uses 191 too. The 183-182 revolt and the capture of Messene belong to achaean-league's ledger and are listed here only as a war. Philip II's and Epaminondas' border arrangements (Dentheliatis, Arcadia) and any Messenian membership of the Hellenic League are not on the pages opened. Sparta (the helot owner) is peloponnesian-league. Counterpart note: 'peloponnesian-league' is the slug eu-01-c uses for 'Sparta (Peloponnesian League)'.
